full_judgment:
2. The facts of the case in brief are that the respondent No.1, Bangladesh Shilpa Bank (BSB), Maijdi Branch, Noakhali as plaintiff filed a suit being Artha Rin Suit No.1 of 1992 in the Court of the then Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, 1st Court, Feni impleading the defendant-respondent No.1 and others for realisation of its outstanding dues amounting to Tk.1,30,40,106.00 with interest and eventually, the said suit was decreed ex-parte on 27.9.1993. After getting the ex-parte decree the decree-holder-Bank in usual course put the decree into execution by filing Artha Rin Execution Case No.3 of 1995. The Artha Rin Adalat on several occasions fixed date for auction sale of the mortgaged property but due to various reasons the property could not be sold in auction and ultimately, the Adalat by its order No. 87 dated 25.2.2003 fixed on 20.4.2003 for auction sale of the mortgaged property and on that date the present appellant, Awlad Hossain became the highest bidder out of total 4 bidders and thereupon, the Adalat directed him to deposit 25% of total bid money within 24 hours. 

 8. On the other hand, Mr. Md. Abdun Nur, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No.1 decree-holder-Bank supports the impugned order dated 07.07.2003 which was, according to him just, correct and proper. Mr. Nur, referring to the provisions of Order XXI, rule 84 of the Code of Civil Procedure submits that rule 84 clearly provides that on every sale of immovable property the person declared to be the purchaser shall pay immediately after such declaration to deposit of 25% of his purchase money to the offer and the Adalat under the legal obligation as per provisions of Order XXI, rule 84 of the Code of Civil Procedure and section 33(2) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 rightly rejected the application of the present appellant for one month time to deposit 25% of the bid money. Mr. Nur also adds that in view of the provision of Order XXI, rule 84 of the Code of Civil Procedure person does not mean 1st bidder or highest bidder, it includes all the bidders. 

 12. Form a combined reading of the above quoted provisions of section 44 of the Ain,2003 it transpires that no Revision or Appeal lies against an interlocutory order of the Artha Rin Adalat but in despite of the provisions of sub-section (ii) of the Ain, 2003 any party being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the order or decree of the Artha Rin Adalat may file appeal before the appellate Court in complying with the provisions of section 41 of the Ain, 2003.
